memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If, however, the sore is unchanged so far as the priest can see, and if black hair has grown in it, the affected person is healed. They are clean, and the priest shall pronounce them clean." - Lev 13:37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Black hair growing in the affected area. That was the sign of life returning — normal, healthy growth appearing where the trouble had been.

Healing shows. Not always immediately, and not always dramatically, but real change produces real evidence.

This is one of the ways we can test what is happening in our own lives. Is anything actually growing? Are there signs of life in the areas where God has been at work? Not perfection — the person here still bore the mark — but genuine, visible growth.

Jesus put it plainly: by their fruit you will recognise them (Matt 7:20). And Paul lists what the Spirit grows in a life: love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control (Gal 5:22-23). Notice these are not achievements to manufacture. They are fruit. They grow where the Spirit is at work, the way black hair grows where healing has come.

If you look at your life over the last few years and see more patience than before, more honesty, a softer heart towards people you once dismissed — that is not nothing. That is evidence. Thank God for it.

And if you see little, do not despair. The Priest is still examining, and He is not finished with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What evidence of genuine growth can you see in your life over recent years?
2. Which fruit of the Spirit is God currently growing in you?
3. Have you thanked God for the healing He has already done?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the growth You have already produced in me, even where I have been slow to notice it. Keep working, and let my life show real evidence of Your Spirit. Amen.
